cases.question: This is a recruiter simulation for a fictional Senior Data Architect search at a growing multi-country mobility business. We need someone who has personally shaped a production data platform. Which experience makes Bolaji a credible candidate, and what did he own?

Source: 20_owner_confirmed_production_scope.txt | Title: OWNER-CONFIRMED PRODUCTION RESPONSIBILITY | Section: OWNER-CONFIRMED PRODUCTION RESPONSIBILITY

Confirmation recorded on November 19, 2026. This is the confirmation date, not a date assigned to the underlying work. Evidence classification: candidate_confirmed.

At Gozem, Bolaji personally designed and operated Pub/Sub and Dataflow in production for the MongoDB CDC pipeline. The owner subsequently clarified that he is both an architect and engineer and personally designed and operated the production services he used. This supersedes the earlier design-only qualification for these services.

For the Gozem Data Hub, Bolaji personally designed and operated AWS EC2 in production.

Bolaji personally set up an AWS S3 bucket in production. Bolaji personally operates an AWS S3 bucket in production, reading data from it and writing data back. This clarification does not identify an employer or project for the S3 bucket and does not establish on-call responsibility.

These clarifications do not add personal Spark Structured Streaming, Apache NiFi or Lakeflow production experience. They do not establish CDC event counts, end-to-end latency or availability. The separately documented streaming-workload average remains a different measurement population.

Source: 00_identity.txt | Title: BOLAJI BALOGOUN - IDENTITY & CONTACT | Section: WHY BOLAJI - VALUE PROPOSITION: | Parent context: BOLAJI BALOGOUN - IDENTITY & CONTACT

Bolaji is a data and AI executive and an impact-driven builder. He does not just set strategy: he architects and deploys the systems himself while leading the team that scales them. He has built data platforms serving millions of users in markets most engineers never touch.

What makes Bolaji different from other senior data and AI candidates:

1. Builder-leader hybrid: at Gozem he led a data organization of 14+ professionals supporting five African operating markets AND still coded, architected, and shipped production systems. Most leaders at this level stop building. Bolaji does both.

2. Self-taught adaptability: he taught himself Google Cloud Platform with zero prior cloud experience and deployed a full production analytics infrastructure within a single quarter because the business needed it, migrating 10+ TB without operational interruption. He learns fast under pressure and delivers.

3. Full-stack data and AI: Bolaji has worked every layer of the data stack, from statistics and econometrics to data engineering, machine learning, AI product delivery, and team leadership. The combination across the entire stack is the differentiator.

4. Real-world African market expertise: he built production systems supporting five African operating markets with real infrastructure constraints, multilingual contexts, and distributed teams, serving millions of real users daily.

Why interview Bolaji for a senior data or AI role:
He combines 10+ years of hands-on technical depth (Python, SQL, GCP, Airflow, LLMs, agentic AI) with proven leadership of a team he grew from 4 to 14+ during the Head of Data period (October 2022 - March 2025). He chartered the Gozem Data Hub serving over 700 people, cut Google Cloud costs by 42.57% in a single quarter, shipped 30+ production AI tools (RAG chatbots, document intelligence, fraud screening, market monitoring), and set governance across 250+ production pipelines. He is equally comfortable writing BigQuery SQL, designing system architecture, mentoring engineers, or presenting to executive leadership.

Source: 90_website_canon_llms_full.txt | Title: Bolaji BALOGOUN · Data Engineer · Data Architect (full content) | Section: Data products at operating scale | Parent context: Bolaji BALOGOUN · Biography

Bolaji architected and led the development of the [Gozem Data Hub](https://www.bolablg.com/experience/gozem-director/#data-hub), a governed operational and analytics platform adopted by 700+ employees, field agents, and partners across five African countries. It provided self-service access to operational applications, analytics, AI tools, and automation. The published case documents React, FastAPI, AWS EC2, BigQuery, MongoDB, Nginx, Docker, Google Cloud Storage, Artifact Registry, and Python.

The data team monitored more than 250 pipelines. Bolaji established governance, observability, and reliability standards across 300+ workflow orchestration, transformation, and metrics-layer assets.

Partnered with HR on workforce planning, hiring business cases, candidate evaluation frameworks, technical assessments, interviews, hiring decisions, onboarding, and performance management. Used **Breezy HR** to manage recruiting.

Used these measures to inform staffing, prioritization, coaching, and resource allocation.

Introduced a domain-based partnership with business leaders that clarified data ownership, strengthened governance, and set clear accountability for KPIs. Made the data team part of recurring operational, strategic, and Growth decisions.
Tools: Breezy HR · Google Workspace · Asana · BigQuery · Looker Studio

evidence.content_preview:
Source: 03_previous_role_gozem_gda.txt | Title: BOLAJI BALOGOUN - PREVIOUS ROLE: GLOBAL DATA ANALYST AT GOZEM | Section: KEY ACHIEVEMENTS: | Parent context: BOLAJI BALOGOUN - PREVIOUS ROLE: GLOBAL DATA ANALYST AT GOZEM

Migrated Gozem's data infrastructure to Google Cloud:
- Situation: the data infrastructure ran on legacy batch processes that could not keep up with growing operational and analytical needs across countries. There was no data warehouse. Bolaji had never worked with GCP or AWS before.
- Action: self-taught Google BigQuery, Cloud Storage, and related tools. Opted for a cloud-first approach to avoid maintenance overhead. Designed a BigQuery-based data warehouse with 50+ scheduled ETL pipelines.
- Tools: Google BigQuery, Google Cloud Storage, Google Dataflow, Apache Airflow, Python.
- Outcome: migrated 10+ TB within a single quarter, without operational interruption, into a fully functional cloud-based analytics infrastructure. Founded the analytics engineering function on top of it.

Automated operational monitoring:
- Situation: operations monitoring relied on a manual recurring job to spot business scenarios across markets, taking up to 2 days of analyst work per cycle.
- Action: automated the workflow within the first 6 months of the role. Python jobs querying PostgreSQL surfaced supply gaps, driver behaviour anomalies, and fraudulent trip patterns into Google Sheets for the operations team.
- Outcome: replaced a 2-day manual job with a 5-15 minute automated cycle.

Automated incentive payments:
- Situation: the agent and partner incentive payment process took multiple days, with manual reviews creating delays, errors, and heavy load on the finance team.
- Action: built automated data pipelines combining predictive analytics and near-real-time monitoring, with structured logs and dispute trails for finance and support.
- Outcome: reduced a multi-day manual process to minutes and facilitated more driver engagement.

Built the fraud patterns database:
- Situation: financial defaults from undetected fraud patterns were eroding margins, with no central knowledge base of known schemes.
- Action: implemented a fraud patterns database fed by automated daily collection monitoring, surfacing anomalies the same day they appeared.
- Outcome: zero unknown financial defaults during the period. Laid the groundwork for the later ML-based fraud screening pipeline.

Marketing segmentation and cohort analysis:
- Situation: marketing campaigns were broadly targeted because the team lacked a structured user profiling layer.
- Action: built a profiling database covering riders and drivers, with RFM segmentation and cohort analysis used by Marketing for targeted campaigns.
- Outcome: supported targeted campaigns and retention analysis. The approximately 9% retention improvement belongs to the separate seasonal driver-retention analysis, not user retention.

Seasonal driver-retention analysis:
- Action: identified driver churn associated with the agricultural season and informed an incentive response.
- Outcome: supported an approximately 9% improvement in driver retention. The measurement interval is not confirmed as quarter-over-quarter.

Business health monitoring and daily insights:
- Situation: country managers and top management lacked a single daily lens on business health across markets.
- Action: consolidated 20+ KPIs into a daily report spanning all business areas, built in Google Sheets and transitioned to Google Data Studio and Tableau after the BigQuery migration.
- Outcome: daily insights presented to country managers and top management, surfacing trends and anomalies for operational decisions.

Built and led a distributed analytics team:
- Action: founded the analytics engineering function and grew a distributed team of 4, delivering automated dashboards, KPI reporting, and weekly market insights.
